keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «가장 걱정스러운 것은 충돌이 꼬리를 무는 연쇄 반응이다(문제)» 와 «지구 주변 우주는 깨끗하게 지켜야 할 공동 자원이다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the problem (the most worrying possibility is a chain reaction of collisions) and the conclusion (the area around Earth is a shared resource that we must keep clean). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why is even a small piece of space junk dangerous?
qs.qko: 왜 아주 작은 우주 쓰레기 조각도 위험한가요?
opts: Objects in low orbit travel at about 28,000 kilometers per hour
Small pieces are covered in poisonous paint
Small pieces fall to Earth every night
evs: Even a small piece is dangerous, because objects in low orbit travel at about 28,000 kilometers per hour.
Many of them are no longer working.
Since the first satellite, Sputnik 1, was launched in 1957, humans have sent thousands of objects into orbit.
why: 본문에 낮은 궤도의 물체는 시속 약 28,000킬로미터로 움직인다고 나와요. 그렇게 빠르면 작은 조각도 우주선을 망가뜨릴 수 있어요.
Objects in low orbit travel at about 28,000 kilometers per hour, so even a small piece can damage a spacecraft.

qs.q: In the text, what does "the stakes are high" mean?
qs.qko: 글에서 «the stakes are high» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
opts: A lot could be lost, because we depend on satellites every day
Satellites are placed very high above the ground
Space agencies are paid a lot of money
evs: Since we depend on satellites for GPS, weather forecasts, and communication, the stakes are high.
Together, they are called space junk or orbital debris.
Look up at the night sky, and you might see a satellite moving slowly among the stars.
why: «the stakes are high» 는 «잃을 것이 많다» 는 뜻이에요. 같은 문장에서 우리가 GPS, 일기 예보, 통신을 위성에 의존한다고 하니, 위성을 못 쓰게 되면 큰 손해를 봐요.
It means a lot could be lost. We depend on satellites for GPS, weather forecasts, and communication.

qs.q: How could a chain reaction make some orbits too dangerous to use?
qs.qko: 연쇄 반응은 어떻게 어떤 궤도를 쓰기 너무 위험하게 만들 수 있나요?
opts: One crash makes debris that causes more crashes, so the debris keeps growing
Old satellites burn up and fill the sky with smoke
The space station fires its engines too often
evs: In 1978, NASA scientist Donald Kessler warned that one collision could create debris that causes more collisions, and so on.
This scenario, now called the Kessler syndrome, could make some orbits too dangerous to use for many years.
The International Space Station sometimes has to fire its engines to move away from approaching debris.
New rules ask companies to bring old satellites down so they burn up in the atmosphere.
why: 한 번의 충돌이 파편을 만들고, 그 파편이 또 다른 충돌을 일으킨다는 경고가 나와요. 이것이 계속되면 어떤 궤도는 오랫동안 쓰기 너무 위험해져요. 두 문장을 이어 봐야 해요.
One collision could create debris that causes more collisions. This Kessler syndrome could make some orbits too dangerous to use for years.

ends: How do nets and robotic arms catch space junk?
그물과 로봇 팔은 어떻게 우주 쓰레기를 잡을까?
What happens when an old satellite burns up in the atmosphere?
낡은 위성이 대기권에서 불타면 어떤 일이 일어날까?
